quotes.text: This controls the allowed types instead of selecting a single default payment method.
For `send_invoice`, customers can select from the eligible payment method types when they pay on the Hosted Invoice Page.
For `charge_automatically`, Stripe attempts payment without first showing the customer a payment method selector.
Stripe also attempts to include the type of the applicable default payment method and filters the result based on eligibility for the invoice.
If you explicitly configure an ineligible type, Stripe might return an error when creating or updating the subscription or finalizing an invoice.

old_evidence.text: If set, a subscription’s `payment_settings.payment_method_types` takes priority over default invoice settings, but only for that specific subscription.

If you enable **Save customer payment information** in the Dashboard invoice settings or the [save_default_payment_method](https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/object.md#subscription_object-payment_settings-save_default_payment_method) parameter of the `Subscription`, any payment method the customer uses to pay the invoice becomes the new default.
A link can only update the payment method on the associated subscription, and can’t change the customer’s default payment method.

findings: The November capture at https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/payment-methods-setting identifies subscription `payment_settings.payment_method_types` as a set of allowed types, not a single default method (new 5-9). It distinguishes `send_invoice` customer choice on the Hosted Invoice Page from `charge_automatically` attempts without an initial selector (new 11-14). Activation, recurring/product support, currency, amount, country and collection method constrain actual eligibility (new 16-21,61-65).

For generated invoices, Stripe starts from Invoice default payment method configuration, attempts to include the applicable default method's type, then filters by eligibility; explicit subscription types take precedence for that subscription and pass to its SetupIntent and invoices (new 25-27). The current source's three-step list at 31-33 conflates type allowance with the individual default attempt priority described separately in old 34-38. Its pitfall at source 27 should say include the default method's type, as new 57-59 does.

The May guide's `save_default_payment_method` sentence at old 40 combines two distinct controls: Dashboard Invoice settings and a parameter on the Subscription. It says a method used to pay becomes 'the new default' but does not identify the destination object for both paths. Current source 37 asserts both make the subscription default, and `wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions-invoices.md` 109 repeats an unqualified subscription-default claim. Correct both to May-only wording: the paid method becomes a new default under those controls; the exact target for each path is unresolved from this capture. Do not infer that both alter the subscription default or that the November guide confirms saving behavior.

The November Dashboard steps document creating a subscription with an emailed manual invoice; its API example creates with an existing Customer, recurring Price, and a restricted key needing subscription_write permission (new 31-55). The May code updates a subscription (old 18-28). These are sample/UI contexts, not evidence that the other operation was removed or that payment succeeded.

The May Dashboard payment-update-link guide is separate from save-default behavior: old 42-61 scopes links to automatically billed subscriptions and says they update only the associated subscription method, not the customer's default; active/past_due/trialing, card-only, single-use and 30-day limits are May-only claims. Current source 39-48 and invoice concept 111 should retain them as dated evidence, not November-confirmed current availability. Link behavior at old 57 does not resolve the default destination in old 40.

The May error section describes possible creation and payment/finalization failures (old 63-70); the November warning uses 'might' for creation, update or finalization if an explicitly configured type is ineligible (new 61-65). Current source 52-54's categorical creation-failure arrow should be narrowed. Root index 7 routes through Stripe index 654/689 to this source and `wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions-invoices.md` 103-111,137. No canonical file was edited.
substantive_changes: Allowed method-type versus selected default identity, collection-method-specific payment flow, default-type inclusion and invoice eligibility filtering are explicit in November (new 9-14,25-27,57-65).

November shows a Dashboard manual-invoice creation path and API create sample, while May shows subscriptions.update; this is a documentation/sample change without proof of operation removal (new 31-55; old 18-28).

The source update must qualify payment-priority and possible error timing, and independently correct May save-default destination overstatement in current source 37 and invoice concept 109; new 1-65 is silent on saving a paid method as default.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May subscriptions.update example, per-subscription type precedence, and separate legacy default_source method-priority point as dated evidence (old 18-38).

Preserve old 40 only at its supported scope: either Dashboard Invoice 'Save customer payment information' or Subscription `save_default_payment_method` may make a paid method 'the new default'; this capture does not say which object each path changes. Current source 37 and invoice concept 109 must lose their unqualified subscription-default destination.

Preserve May payment-update-link restrictions (old 42-61) as dated and distinct from save-default; their associated-subscription-only effect at old 57 must not be transferred to the separate settings in old 40.
conflicts: Current source 37 and invoice concept 109 assert a subscription-default target for saved payment methods. Old 40 says only 'the new default' after either Dashboard Invoice setting or Subscription parameter; new 1-65 omits the topic. Narrow both pages and mark target unresolved, as prior review required.

Current source 31-33 collapses allowed types, invoice defaults and legacy default_source into one payment-priority ladder, whereas old 34-38 and new 25-27 separate type selection from individual default attempt priority and eligibility filtering.

Current source 52-54 says ineligibility leads to subscription creation failure. New 65 says it might error at creation, update or finalization; old 65-70 also includes payment-time failure. Preserve the modal and stage boundaries.
unresolved_questions: Which default destination is changed by the Dashboard Invoice setting versus Subscription `payment_settings.save_default_payment_method` is not established by old 40 or new 1-65; a dedicated current settings/API source would be needed to resolve it.

November does not address Dashboard payment-update links, their current restrictions, legacy default_source or save-default behavior. Omission is not deprecation or confirmation of continued availability.
No account-specific eligibility, customer payment attempt, successful collection or final invoice outcome was observed in the assigned captures.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/payment-methods-setting, subscription `payment_settings.payment_method_types` controls allowed types rather than an individual default method (new 5-9). `send_invoice` presents eligible choices on the Hosted Invoice Page, while `charge_automatically` attempts collection without first showing a selector; activation and invoice eligibility still constrain choices (new 11-27,57-65). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]] summarizes May subscription-update, priority, save-default and update-link material (old 18-61), but its source line 37 wrongly specifies the subscription as default destination for both save controls. Old 40 only calls it 'the new default'; the object target for each control is unresolved.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/payment-methods-setting, November's substantive clarification concerns type identity, collection-method flow and invoice eligibility (new 9-14,25-27,61-65). The Dashboard create path and API example do not deprecate May's update example (new 31-55; old 18-28). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]] should separate type precedence from default attempt priority, narrow categorical error timing, and preserve May-only update-link details as dated. Crucially, source 37 and reciprocal invoice concept 109 must no longer say both Dashboard Invoice settings and Subscription `save_default_payment_method` set the subscription default: old 40 names both controls but only says 'new default', and the new guide is silent. Neither UI sample nor API snippet proves successful billing.
